title: A Classification of Hirota-Integrable Supersymmetric Bilinear KdV-Type Equations
abstract: We present a classification of supersymmetric bilinear KdV-type equations admitting unconstrained three-super-soliton solutions. Extending Hirota's classical three-soliton criterion to the supersymmetric setting, we derive the complete bosonic and fermionic compatibility conditions governing the existence of three-super-soliton solutions. We prove that every supersymmetric bilinear KdV-type equation possesses unconstrained one- and two-super-soliton solutions, whereas three-super-soliton solutions exist only when eight integrability conditions are satisfied. These conditions provide a supersymmetric analogue of Hirota's classical integrability criterion and naturally recover the fermionic relations previously introduced by Carstea, revealing their structural origin. As a consequence, we classify the supersymmetric extensions of Hirota bilinear KdV-type equations and show that only a subset of Hietarinta's classical classification remains valid in the unrestricted supersymmetric framework.
summary: This paper classifies supersymmetric bilinear KdV-type equations by deriving the necessary algebraic conditions for the existence of three-super-soliton solutions. By extending Hirota's classical criterion, the authors establish that integrability requires satisfying eight specific compatibility conditions. This work provides a unified mathematical framework for studying soliton dynamics in supersymmetric field theories.
main_problem: The paper aims to classify supersymmetric bilinear Korteweg-de Vries (KdV)-type equations by determining the necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of unconstrained three-super-soliton solutions.
main_result: Three-super-soliton solutions exist only when eight specific integrability conditions are satisfied, providing a supersymmetric analogue to Hirota's classical integrability criterion.
method: The authors extend Hirota's classical three-soliton criterion to the supersymmetric setting, utilizing the super-Hirota bilinear method and analyzing the algebraic compatibility conditions derived from the soliton ansatz.
model_or_system: The primary model is the integrable N=1 supersymmetric extension of the KdV equation, formulated using superfields $\Phi$ on superspace $(x, t, 	heta)$. The analysis is conducted through the super-Hirota bilinear representation.
key_observables: The existence and structure of one-, two-, and three-super-soliton solutions, and the resulting bosonic and fermionic compatibility conditions.
important_parameters: The structure of the polynomial $P$ governing the dispersion relation, and the fermionic wave numbers ($\kappa_1, \kappa_2, \kappa_3$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the $	au$-function representation and investigates the difference between 'Strong' and 'Weak' Hirota integrability.

paper_structure: The paper first establishes the supersymmetric KdV equation and its super-Hirota bilinear form. It then analyzes the one- and two-soliton solutions, showing their general existence. The core of the work focuses on deriving the necessary eight compatibility conditions required for the three-super-soliton solution, leading to the classification.
why_interesting: While focused on classical integrable systems, the systematic extension of integrability criteria (like Hirota's method) into a supersymmetric framework provides powerful mathematical tools applicable to quantum field theories and quantum many-body systems exhibiting supersymmetry.
